new.maintxt: With professional experience in web design and UI/UX development, I specialize in delivering responsive, user-focused digital experiences for web and mobile, as well as a variety of design and visual projects.
new.abouttit: EVERY CHALLENGE IS AN OPPORTUNITY FOR GROWTH.
new.abouttxt: I VIEW EVERY CHALLENGE AS A VALUABLE OPPERTUNITY TO STRENGTHEN MY SKILLS, ENHANCE ADAPTABILITY, AND CREATE GREATER IMPACT.
new.imtxt: I deliver company objectives through web and digital design by creating modern, user-friendly and responsive visual solutions. Responsive visual solutions, while collaborating with Cross-functional teams, developers and planners—to ensure clarity And engagement and alignment with project goals.

skills.webdesign: In my web design, I implement user-centered responsive layouts and effective navigation to ensure accessibility. Additionally, I incorporate interactive elements as supplementary features to enhance the overall user experience.
skills.appdesign: In my app design process, I take into account user needs and behavior patterns, service objectives, information architecture, platform-specific requirements, visual consistency, accessibility, and technical constraints to create effective and user-centered solutions.
skills.creative: I create designs that align with the client’s goals and vision, utilizing a wide range of creative tools. My skills span across 2D and 3D design, video production and editing and I am also proficient in presentation and various other forms of visual design.
skills.uiux: I deliver designs that encompass the entire process — from planning and prototyping to user experience design. Using XD and Figma, I create effective design prototypes and facilitate smooth collaboration between planners and developers. With a solid understanding of UI/UX principles, I meticulously refine every detail to achieve a polished and complete result.
skills.development: I continue to study development and strive to grow in line with the latest front-end trends. In addition to a solid foundation in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, I develop web front-end projects using various libraries. Through close collaboration with back-end developers, I contribute to building efficient web structures by understanding data binding and overall architecture.

program.xd: I specialize in structuring and designing web and app prototypes using Adobe XD, facilitating seamless communication between planners and developers. During my work on Samsung Electronics projects, I effectively utilized XD in an environment where Figma was restricted, establishing an efficient system for design sharing and collaboration. Beyond visual execution, I leverage design thinking — testing prototypes, identifying issues from the user’s perspective, and developing creative, insight-driven solutions to deliver refined results.
program.ps: I primarily use Photoshop to enhance the visual precision and completeness of prototypes. Beyond simple editing, I utilize it as a tool for visual problem-solving — adjusting color, texture, and balance to deliver refined visual solutions that align with client needs and brand identity.
program.ai: I utilize Adobe Illustrator to create vector-based icons, logos, and illustrations, maintaining precise shapes and lines to ensure high-quality design output. For logos, I transfer designs to XD for integration into prototypes without resolution loss, and I also apply Illustrator in producing various print materials such as business cards, banners, and brochures.
program.pr: I have produced high-quality video content using Premiere Pro, including editing, cutting, color grading, and subtitle insertion. By considering project intent and storytelling, I ensure that the message is communicated clearly. For several projects, including opening videos for the HR team, I imported After Effects files, edited them and delivered final outputs using Media Encoder.
program.ae: I have created motion graphics, animation effects, and typography using After Effects, enhancing both engagement and message delivery in video content. I carefully craft motions and visual emphasis according to project intent, integrating them into Premiere Pro projects and for shorter videos, I sometimes produce final outputs directly from After Effects.
program.fg: I have used Figma to create UI/UX designs and prototypes, initially exploring it as a tool for real-time collaboration and efficient design review with team members. In practice, I leveraged design systems and components to maintain consistency across projects and at a startup, I led UI planning, facilitating immediate communication and alignment between planners and developers.
program.vue: I utilize Vue.js to systematically structure UI components and implement intuitive, seamless user interactions. By bridging frontend logic with design, I deliver both visual and functional experiences. Vue.js was primarily used in the development of Samsung’s HR system, offering excellent compatibility and enabling efficient component maintenance.
program.html: I am proficient in structuring web pages and content using HTML. By applying semantic markup, I ensure accessibility and SEO, and I integrate HTML with CSS and JavaScript to build dynamic web pages. My foundational knowledge of HTML allowed me to adapt quickly to Vue.js-based templates and I have also built web pages using vanilla HTML in past portfolio projects.
program.css: I utilize CSS to systematically design web page layouts and styles. By implementing responsive design with media queries, I ensure an optimal user experience across devices. I integrate CSS with HTML structure to deliver both visual quality and functionality and I effectively apply animations and interactive elements in line with current design trends.
program.js: I have used JavaScript to implement dynamic functionality and user interactions on web pages. Through DOM manipulation, event handling, and data binding, I have developed functional and intuitive web environments while continuously improving my skills. I have built maintainable and scalable web applications using frameworks such as Vue.js and can leverage both vanilla JS and various libraries and frameworks to implement efficient and extensible web solutions.
program.ts: TypeScript is not just a language, but a core tool for building stable and scalable frontend solutions. I recently began learning it and applied it to develop a new web portfolio site. Compared to JavaScript, it allowed me to fully leverage development tools and quickly identify errors, making coding and debugging much more efficient. I plan to continue using TypeScript actively to create stable and maintainable web applications.
program.flu: I used Flutter to develop cross-platform mobile applications for iOS and Android. Although the widget-based architecture was initially unfamiliar, I learned it through self-study and hands-on practice, creating individual widgets in a component-like structure similar to Vue.js. I also utilized Google’s design-guided widgets and customized them as needed to implement the UI. The framework proved efficient and practical, allowing me to develop apps for both platforms simultaneously.
program.php: I have experience learning and understanding PHP for web applications and server-side functionality. On GnuBoard (G5)-based sites, I studied server-side logic such as user management, bulletin boards, and email delivery, learning and utilizing PHP to enable data integration between backend and frontend and to implement dynamic features. This experience allowed me to understand how to operate web services reliably and handle user requests.

talent.maintit: Is an outdated and inefficient HR system still acceptable?
talent.subtit: The project aimed to transition an HR system previously managed by a subsidiary into an internally operated platform, while modernizing and elevating the overall user experience.

myrole.top: Independently owned the end-to-end product cycle from requirements analysis → IA → UI/UX design → prototyping → front-end implementation
middle: Identified missing requirements through rapid prototyping (Adobe XD)
Established a brand guideline including logo, color system, and UI components
Designed UX enhancements such as optimized modal flows and feedback interactions
Structured differentiated interfaces based on admin vs. user permissions
Ensured high implementation accuracy by being directly involved in the development handoff and publishing process

problem.top: Is an outdated and inefficient HR system still acceptable?
middle: HR tasks operated separately across 4 different platforms
Duplicate data entry required for both users and managers
Outdated UI with poor usability and confusing workflows
Mobile access blocked due to security concerns → Desktop-only optimization required
Increasing maintenance costs
problem.bottom: Support, approval, training management, and reporting — none of it could be handled in one place.

object.top: Integrated the degree application process into a single unified system and modernized the UI/UX to enhance user productivity and administrative efficiency.
middle: Integrate all HR-related features into One Unified Platform
Provide differentiated permissions and views based on user roles
Improve readability, accessibility, and usability following modern UI/UX standards
Shorten task completion time, reduce errors, and cut maintenance costs
Build a Team-wide UI/UX Design System
Consolidated 4 separate systems into one platform
Role-based customization for users and administrators
Clear and intuitive step-by-step workflows
Established a new, scalable UI/UX Design System
Improved data flow and operational sustainability
solution.bottom: Built a platform where all HR training operations are completed in one place.

approach.top: With almost no existing planning documentation, I established and led the entire design process.

bodytwo: Compiled screen requirements myself due to limited planning resources
Created logo, defined titles, and standardized color system
Structured screen layout based on desktop-first UX
Defined modal behavior, input flows, and feedback UI
Handled full transition from XD to Web implementation

approach.bottom: I transformed vague needs into a structured design strategy and then reverse-engineered it into functional requirements.

one.txt: I reviewed reference websites provided by the planner to understand the project direction and expected UX style. From the provided benchmarks, I extracted key content structures and the initial Information Architecture (IA).

two.tit: Defining Screen Inventory & Structuring the IA
two.txt: The timeline was tight — the entire project had to be completed within 3 months. So I quickly listed all necessary screens aligned with the actual service workflow. By categorizing features and reviewing duplicated or missing content, I established the foundational IA framework.

four.txt: To ensure smooth progress during the screen design phase, I first established the core brand assets such as the logo, titles, and color system. I refreshed the legacy color palette to align with modern visual trends and set up a style guide. I also structured core UI components, including modals and buttons, with SCSS-based implementation in mind from the start.

one.txt: To create a unified system called My Talent from the existing Talent Fair, a new logo mark was introduced. The word “Talent” was retained from the previous system, while “My” was designed in a matching style to create a cohesive brand identity.

two.txt: The overall design concept was unified under a single primary color, while subtle changes were introduced through the balanced use of outer and inner shadows. For emphasis elements, I intentionally avoided red tones and instead used purple to create a distinct and differentiated visual identity.

three.txt: Given the nature of the web platform and its deployment within Samsung’s internal environment, Samsung One UI Gothic (긴 고딕) was selected as the primary typeface. It provides excellent readability with well-balanced letter spacing, making it particularly suitable for content-heavy screens with numerous input fields. Its wide range of font weights also allows for a clear and flexible visual hierarchy. The default body text size was set to 16px to ensure accessibility and readability. Typography scale was systemically applied—larger font sizes and weights were used for table content to enhance visual separation. Based on the core body style, titles, subtitles, and the GNB were designed with distinct levels of emphasis while maintaining consistency throughout the interface. Page titles were emphasized using an underline style, providing a clear visual anchor and a consistent identity across pages. Subtitles were displayed in a structured list format, enabling users to quickly recognize and navigate through different sections. Instructional or descriptive text included icons or markers to highlight informational intent. Hyperlinks that direct to external pages or triggering additional actions were designed using the primary color and shadow accents, reinforcing their clickability through visual affordance.

four.txt: Tables are the most frequently used component in this system, so the design focused on enhancing both usability and maintainability.
content: Vertical padding was set to 10px to ensure comfortable readability across various font sizes.

Color was applied to table headers to clearly distinguish them from the body area. For community-related sections, the primary blue color was used to bring more liveliness and refresh the user experience.
Input tables adopt a gray-tone color scheme to reduce eye fatigue, and placeholders were used to guide user input more intuitively.
Instead of a traditional table layout, a Flex Grid structure was implemented for greater flexibility in future updates and maintenance.

five.txt: The primary button color was set to a blue tone, while the temporary save buttons used a secondary purple color, and payment-related query buttons were highlighted in green. Due to company guidelines prohibiting red, reset buttons were designed in black, and selection buttons in white. Shadows were applied to all buttons to create a sense of depth and to reinforce the visual prominence of the clickable elements.

six.tit: Visual-first UI Design with High-Fidelity Prototyping
six.txt: Rather than investing time in low-fidelity wireframes, I directly developed high-fidelity prototypes using Adobe XD. Through agile iteration, I incorporated planning feedback into the design in real time, which helped accelerate decision-making and improve completeness.

seven.tit: One-Stop Execution from Design to Front-End Publishing
seven.txt: I continued beyond UI design to define interaction flows such as modal behavior and detailed feedback responses, and I personally carried out the front-end publishing. This ensured that the final implementation accurately reflected the design intent and maintained a high standard of UI quality.
